gloss: be straight, level, right; upright; straightness, equity; level ground
summary: Straight and level: a way that runs on without turning to the right or the left, feet and wings held straight, rough ground made a plain. From this the root says what is right: “right in the eyes” of someone is what he approves, and the measure scripture presses is what is right in the eyes of Yahweh against what is right in a man's own eyes. The adjective יָשָׁר is upright, of men whose heart and way are straight, and of Yahweh himself and his word; the nouns are straightness of way and heart (יֹשֶׁר), equity, the even justice by which Yahweh will judge the world (מֵישָׁרִים), and level ground or the plateau east of the Jordan (מִישׁוֹר). Akkadian ešēru “be straight, go well”, išaru “straight, just” and mīšaru “justice” carry the same two sides.

words.gloss: straight, level; right, pleasing; upright, just
words.summary: About a hundred and twenty times. Most often in “do what is right in the eyes of Yahweh”, the verdict on Israel's kings, and as “the upright”, those whose heart and way are straight, beside the blameless and the righteous; Yahweh himself is upright, and so are his word, his ways and his precepts.

senses.gloss: straight, level (of a way, feet, wings)
senses.definition: Running straight on, without bend or turning: a way that leads directly to its end without stumbling, feet or wings held straight.

evidence.note: The living creatures' “feet were straight feet (רֶגֶל יְשָׁרָה)”.
“Their wings straight (יְשָׁרוֹת), one toward the other.”
“He led them by a straight way (בְּדֶרֶךְ יְשָׁרָה) to go to a city of habitation.”
“I will lead them … in a straight way (בְּדֶרֶךְ יָשָׁר) in which they shall not stumble.”
A fast “to seek from him a straight way for us and for our little ones”.
“The way of the sluggard is a hedge of thorns, but the path of the upright is a raised highway.”
“The path of the righteous is evenness; O upright one (יָשָׁר), you level the track of the righteous.”

senses.gloss: right (in someone's eyes), what he approves
senses.definition: With “in the eyes of”: what someone judges right and approves. Above all, doing “what is right in the eyes of Yahweh”, the measure by which each king of Judah is judged, set against doing what is right in one's own eyes.

evidence.note: “You shall not do according to all that we do here today, each man all that is right in his own eyes.”
“That it may go well with you … when you do the good and the right (הַטּוֹב וְהַיָּשָׁר) in the eyes of Yahweh your God.”
“You shall do the right and the good in the eyes of Yahweh.”
“To do the right in the eyes of Yahweh your God.”
“If you listen carefully to the voice of Yahweh your God and do the right in his eyes … I am Yahweh your healer.”
“In those days there was no king in Israel; each man did what was right in his own eyes”; again at the end of the book (Jdg 21:25).
“The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but he who listens to counsel is wise.”
“Every way of a man is right in his own eyes, but Yahweh weighs the hearts.”
“There is a way that is right before a man, but its end is the ways of death”; repeated at Pro 16:25.
David “kept my commandments and walked after me with all his heart, to do only the right in my eyes”.
“Asa did the right in the eyes of Yahweh, like David his father.”
Hezekiah “did the right in the eyes of Yahweh, according to all that David his father had done”.
Josiah “did the right in the eyes of Yahweh … and did not turn aside to the right or to the left”.
Ahaz “did not do the right in the eyes of Yahweh his God, like David his father”.
The Gibeonites to Joshua: “Do to us as seems good and right in your eyes.”
Jeremiah: “Do with me as is good and right in your eyes.”
“Choose the best and the fittest (וְהַיָּשָׁר) of your master's sons.”

senses.definition: Of a man, his heart or his way: straight, without crookedness or deceit, keeping to what Yahweh calls right; as a plural noun, “the upright”, set beside the blameless and the righteous and against the wicked and the treacherous.

evidence.note: “That man was blameless and upright (תָּם וְיָשָׁר), and feared God and turned away from evil”; also Job 1:8; 2:3.
“Mark the blameless and see the upright, for the end of that man is peace.”
“Be glad in Yahweh and rejoice, righteous ones; and shout, all upright of heart (יִשְׁרֵי־לֵב).”
“My shield is upon God, who saves the upright of heart.”
The wicked bend the bow “to shoot in the dark at the upright of heart”.
“Do good, Yahweh, to the good, and to the upright in their hearts.”
“The integrity of the upright guides them, but the crookedness of the treacherous destroys them.”
“The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of the upright will flourish.”
“A wicked man hardens his face, but the upright, he establishes his way.”
“An unjust man is an abomination to the righteous, and one upright in the way is an abomination to the wicked.”
“The devious is an abomination to Yahweh, but his counsel is with the upright.”
“The upright will dwell in the land.”
“The godly has perished from the land, and there is none upright among men.”
“Where were the upright cut off?”
“God made man upright, but they have sought out many schemes.”
Balaam of Israel: “Let me die the death of the upright, and let my end be like his.”
Achish to David: “As Yahweh lives, you have been upright.”
“Your heart is not straight (εὐθεῖα) before God”: the Septuagint's word for יָשָׁר.

senses.gloss: upright, just (of Yahweh, his word and ways)
senses.definition: Of Yahweh: straight and just, without crookedness in what he does; of his word, ways, precepts and judgments: right, true to what they say.

evidence.note: “The Rock, his work is perfect, for all his ways are justice; a God of faithfulness and without injustice, righteous and upright is he.”
“To declare that Yahweh is upright; my rock, and there is no unrighteousness in him.”
“Good and upright is Yahweh; therefore he instructs sinners in the way.”
“Righteous are you, Yahweh, and upright are your judgments.”
“The precepts of Yahweh are right, rejoicing the heart.”
“The word of Yahweh is upright, and all his work is in faithfulness.”
“The ways of Yahweh are right, and the righteous walk in them, but transgressors stumble in them.”
“You gave them right judgments and true laws.”
Wisdom's words “are all … right to those who find knowledge”.
“Will you not cease to make crooked the straight ways (τὰς ὁδοὺς … τὰς εὐθείας) of the Lord?”, the words of Hos 14:10.

evidence.locator: Deu.12.8, יָשָׁר → ἀρεστόν; Deu.6.18; Deu.12.28; Exo.15.26 → ἀρεστόν

evidence.note: “I always do the things pleasing (τὰ ἀρεστά) to him.”
“We keep his commandments and do the things pleasing before him (τὰ ἀρεστὰ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ)”: the Septuagint's words for doing what is right in Yahweh's eyes.

evidence.locator: Psa.107.7, יְשָׁרָה → εὐθεῖαν; Psa.19.9; Ezr.8.21; 1Sa.12.23; Pro.20.11 → εὐθύς

evidence.note: “Forsaking the straight way (εὐθεῖαν ὁδόν) they went astray, following the way of Balaam”: as those “who forsake the paths of uprightness” (Pro 2:13).

parallels.note: “Righteous”: the righteous and the upright of heart rejoice together; Yahweh is righteous and upright.
“Good”: “the good and the right in the eyes of Yahweh”.

opposites.note: “Wicked”: the house of the wicked against the tent of the upright.
“Treacherous”: the integrity of the upright against the crookedness of the treacherous.
“Devious, turned aside”: an abomination to Yahweh, whose counsel is with the upright.

phrases.gloss: do the right in the eyes of Yahweh
each man does what is right in his own eyes
the book of the upright (Jashar), a lost book of songs

evidence.note: “Is it not written in the book of the upright?” of the sun standing still.
David's lament over Saul and Jonathan, “written in the book of the upright”.

words.gloss: go straight; be right, pleasing; make straight, level, direct
words.summary: Twenty-five times. The qal is to go straight on, and, far more often, to be right in someone's eyes, to please him; once to be upright. The piel makes a way straight or level and leads straight on; the pual is laid level, the hiphil makes straight. The qal at Job 37:3 (יִשְׁרֵהוּ “he lets it loose”, of thunder) is the verb שָׁרָה “loose”, filed here by spelling.

stems.gloss: go straight; be right, pleasing (in someone's eyes); be upright

senses.definition: Of a way taken: to keep straight on, turning neither to the right nor to the left.

evidence.note: “The cows went straight (וַיִּשַּׁרְנָה) on the way to Beth-shemesh … and did not turn aside to the right or to the left.”

senses.definition: With “in the eyes of”: to seem right to someone, to please him, so that he approves and acts on it.

evidence.note: Samson of the Philistine woman: “Get her for me, for she is right in my eyes (יָשְׁרָה בְעֵינָי).”
Michal loved David, “and the thing was right in his eyes”: it pleased Saul.
“The word was right in the eyes of Absalom and of all the elders of Israel.”
Hiram saw the cities Solomon had given him, “and they were not right in his eyes”.
The potter made the clay into another vessel, “as it was right in the eyes of the potter to make”.
“I made the earth … and I give it to whom it is right in my eyes.”
Balak: “Perhaps it will be right in the eyes of God that you curse them for me from there.”

senses.definition: Of the soul: to be straight within, the opposite of being puffed up.

evidence.note: “Behold, puffed up, his soul is not upright in him; but the righteous shall live by his faithfulness”; the second half is quoted at Rom 1:17; Gal 3:11; Heb 10:38.

stems.gloss: make straight, level; lead straight, direct; count right

senses.definition: To make a way straight or level, removing what bends or blocks it; of Yahweh, to make a man's paths straight before him.

evidence.note: “Prepare in the wilderness the way of Yahweh; make straight (יַשְּׁרוּ) in the desert a highway for our God”; quoted of John at Mat 3:3; Mar 1:3; Luk 3:4; Joh 1:23.
To Cyrus: “I will go before you and make the swellings level (אֲיַשֵּׁר, Ketiv the hiphil).”
“I have stirred him up in righteousness, and I will make all his ways straight; he shall build my city and send out my exiles.”
“In all your ways know him, and he will make your paths straight.”
“The righteousness of the blameless makes his way straight, but the wicked falls by his own wickedness.”
“Make his paths straight (εὐθείας ποιεῖτε)”, Isa 40:3 of John the Baptist.
John: “I am a voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight (εὐθύνατε) the way of the Lord.”

senses.gloss: go straight on; lead straight, direct
senses.definition: To keep one's course straight, or to direct something straight to where it should go.

evidence.note: Folly calls “to those who pass by, who go straight on (הַמְיַשְּׁרִים) their paths”.
“A man of understanding goes straight (יְיַשֶּׁר־לָכֶת).”
Hezekiah stopped the upper outlet of Gihon “and directed them (וַיַּישְּׁרֵם) down to the west side of the city of David”.

senses.definition: To hold something to be right.

evidence.note: “Therefore all your precepts concerning all things I count right (יִשָּׁרְתִּי); every false way I hate.”

senses.definition: Of gold overlay: laid evenly over carving.

evidence.note: Cherubim, palms and flowers carved on the doors, overlaid “with gold laid evenly (מְיֻשָּׁר) over the carving”.

senses.definition: To make a way straight before someone; of the eyes, to keep them straight ahead.

evidence.note: “Let your eyes look forward, and let your eyelids make straight (יַיְשִׁרוּ) before you.”
“Yahweh, lead me in your righteousness because of my enemies; make your way straight (הַיְשַׁר, Qere) before me.” Not counted in the brief's tokens.

evidence.locator: יָשַׁר → ηὐθύνθη ×2, εὐθύνθη ×1, κατευθύνοντας ×1 (the brief's count); also Jdg.14.3 → εὐθύς; 2Sa.17.4; 1Ch.13.4 → εὐθής

evidence.note: “Make straight (εὐθύνατε) the way of the Lord”, Isa 40:3.

words.gloss: level ground, plain; the plateau (east of the Jordan); uprightness, equity
words.summary: Level ground, where chariots can fight and feet do not stumble; with the article, “the plateau” of Moab north of the Arnon, given to Reuben; and in the psalms and prophets, the evenness of just judgment.

senses.definition: Ground without hills or rough places; what rugged ground or a mountain becomes when it is levelled; figuratively, the even ground where a man stands firm or walks without stumbling.

evidence.note: “Their gods are gods of the hills … but let us fight them in the plain (בַּמִּישׁוֹר), and surely we shall be stronger than they”; again in v. 25.
“Every valley shall be lifted up and every mountain and hill made low, and the rugged (הֶעָקֹב) shall become level ground (לְמִישׁוֹר)”; quoted at Luk 3:5.
“I will make darkness light before them, and crooked places (מַעֲקַשִּׁים) level ground.”
“Who are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you shall become a plain.”
Jerusalem as “dweller of the valley, rock of the plain”.
“My foot stands on level ground; in the assemblies I will bless Yahweh.”
“Teach me your way, Yahweh, and lead me in a level path because of my enemies.”
“Teach me to do your will … let your good spirit lead me in a level land.”
Isa 40:4: “the crooked shall become straight (εἰς εὐθεῖαν), and the rough ways smooth.”

senses.definition: With the article, the tableland east of the Dead Sea from the Arnon north to Heshbon, the cities of Sihon given to Reuben, where the city of refuge Bezer lay.

evidence.note: “All the cities of the plateau and all Gilead and all Bashan.”
“Bezer in the wilderness, in the land of the plateau, for the Reubenites.”
“From Aroer on the edge of the valley of Arnon … and all the plateau of Medeba to Dibon.”
“Judgment has come on the land of the plateau, on Holon, Jahzah and Mephaath.”
Uzziah “had much cattle, both in the lowland and in the plateau”.

senses.definition: The evenness of just judgment and right conduct: judging the poor without favour, the sceptre of a righteous kingdom, a priest's walk with God.

evidence.note: The shoot of Jesse “shall judge the poor with righteousness, and decide with equity (בְּמִישׁוֹר) for the meek of the earth”.
“Your throne, God, is for ever and ever; a sceptre of uprightness (שֵׁבֶט מִישֹׁר) is the sceptre of your kingdom”; quoted of the Son at Heb 1:8.
“You will judge the peoples with equity and lead the nations on the earth.”
Levi: “he walked with me in peace and uprightness, and turned many from iniquity.”
“A sceptre of uprightness (εὐθύτητος) is the sceptre of your kingdom.”

evidence.locator: Psa.45.7, מִישֹׁר → εὐθύτητος; Psa.26.12 → εὐθύτητι; Ecc.12.10, יֹשֶׁר → εὐθύτητος

evidence.note: Psa 45:7 quoted of the Son: “ῥάβδος εὐθύτητος ἡ ῥάβδος τῆς βασιλείας σου.”

words.gloss: equity, uprightness; what is right; smoothly
words.summary: Always plural, מֵישָׁרִים. Most often the equity with which Yahweh judges the peoples, beside צֶדֶק; also upright words and dealings, and, of wine, going down smoothly.

senses.definition: Even, impartial justice, especially Yahweh's judgment of the world and its peoples.

evidence.note: “He will judge the world in righteousness; he will judge the peoples with equity (בְּמֵישָׁרִים).”
“Say among the nations, Yahweh reigns … he will judge the peoples with equity”; and “he comes to judge the earth” (v. 13).
“Before Yahweh, for he comes to judge the earth; he will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with equity.”
“The strength of the king loves justice; you have established equity.”
“When I take the appointed time, I will judge with equity.”
“Do you judge with equity, sons of man?”
“Let my vindication come from your presence; let your eyes see what is right.”
“He will judge the world in righteousness by a man whom he has appointed”, the words of Psa 9:9; 96:13; 98:9.

senses.gloss: uprightness, upright things (in word and dealing)
senses.definition: What is right and straight in speech and conduct; once, the terms of an agreement made between kings.

evidence.note: “To receive instruction in wise dealing, righteousness and justice and uprightness (וּמֵשָׁרִים).”
Wisdom: “the opening of my lips will be right things.”
“My inward parts will rejoice when your lips speak right things.”
“He who walks righteously and speaks uprightly” shall dwell on high.
“I, Yahweh, speak righteousness, I declare right things.”
“You test the heart and are pleased with uprightness.”
“The path of the righteous is evenness (מֵישָׁרִים).”
The daughter of the king of the south comes to the king of the north “to make an agreement (מֵישָׁרִים)”.
“Rightly (מֵישָׁרִים) do they love you.”

senses.definition: Of wine, going down evenly and smoothly.

evidence.note: “Do not look at wine when it is red … when it goes down smoothly (בְּמֵישָׁרִים).”
“Like the best wine, going down smoothly for my beloved.”

senses.definition: The straightness of a way, set against crooked and dark ways.

evidence.note: “Who forsake the paths of straightness (אָרְחוֹת יֹשֶׁר) to walk in the ways of darkness, … whose paths are crooked” (vv. 13–15).
“I have taught you in the way of wisdom; I have led you in tracks of straightness.”
“Forsaking the straight way they went astray”, as Pro 2:13.

senses.definition: Straightness of heart and speech: honesty, integrity before God and men.

evidence.note: “If you walk before me as David your father walked, in integrity of heart and in uprightness (וּבְיֹשֶׁר).”
“Not for your righteousness or for the uprightness of your heart are you going in to possess their land.”
“I will thank you with uprightness of heart.”
“Let integrity and uprightness preserve me, for I wait for you.”
“He who walks in his uprightness fears Yahweh, but he who is crooked in his ways despises him.”
“My words are the uprightness of my heart.”
“How forceful are words of uprightness!”
“In the uprightness of my heart I have freely offered all these things.”
“Words of truth written in uprightness.”

senses.definition: What is right or fitting toward someone.

evidence.note: “One scatters and increases still; another withholds more than is right (מִיֹּשֶׁר), only to want.”
“To strike nobles is against what is right.”
A messenger, an interpreter, “to declare to man what is right for him (יָשְׁרוֹ)”.

words.summary: Once, in “uprightness of heart”; the same as יֹשֶׁר.

senses.definition: Straightness of heart toward God.

evidence.note: Solomon: David “walked before you in faithfulness and in righteousness and in uprightness of heart (וּבְיִשְׁרַת לֵבָב) with you”.

words.gloss: Sharon, a plain of pasture; Lasharon
words.summary: Always with the article but once: the coastal plain north of Joppa, a land of pasture and flowers set beside Carmel and Lebanon; also a pastureland east of the Jordan (1Ch 5:16), and the town Lasharon (Jos 12:18). It is taken as “the level land”, as מִישׁוֹר, but scripture never calls it level, only pasture, so its tie to the root rests on the form alone. A place, so it has no name entry.

senses.definition: A plain of pasture and flowers, whose glory is set with Lebanon and Carmel.

evidence.note: “The glory of Lebanon shall be given to it, the splendour of Carmel and Sharon; they shall see the glory of Yahweh.”
“Sharon shall be a pasture for flocks, and the valley of Achor a resting place for herds, for my people who have sought me.”
“Sharon is like the Arabah.”
“I am a flower of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.”
“Over the herds pasturing in Sharon was Shitrai the Sharonite.”
The Gadites dwelt “in all the pasturelands of Sharon”, east of the Jordan.
“The king of Lasharon (לַשָּׁרוֹן), one.”
“All who dwelt at Lydda and Sharon (Σάρωνα) saw him and turned to the Lord.”

words.summary: Once, of Shitrai, David's overseer of the herds in Sharon; its tie to the root is Sharon's, which rests on the form alone.

senses.definition: A man of Sharon.

evidence.note: “Shitrai the Sharonite (הַשָּׁרוֹנִי).”

“righteous one; straight one”

cognates.gloss: be gentle, tractable, easy; (II) make easy, make a man's way smooth; ease (opposite of hardship)
cognates.note: The sounds match (Arabic s for š, as the Aramaic shows), and “make his way easy or smooth” is near the piel's “make straight a way”; Akkadian ešēru is also used of an easy birth, as Arabic ʾaysarat “she had an easy birth”. But the Arabic's core is ease, not straightness or right, and the same root gives yasār “left hand”, so it is recorded as possible only.

evidence.note: “He (God) made it, or rendered it, easy … he made his condition, or his way or course, easy, or smooth.”

evidence.note: “She brought forth with ease; she had an easy birth.”
Compares Arabic يَسِير “easy, plain, simple”.

doctrine.statement: Moses told Israel that in the land they should no longer do “each man all that is right in his own eyes”, but “the good and the right in the eyes of Yahweh your God” (Deu 12:8, 28; 6:18); healing and blessing were promised to those who do “the right in his eyes” (Exo 15:26). The judges end in the opposite: “there was no king in Israel; each man did what was right in his own eyes” (Jdg 17:6; 21:25). Proverbs gives the reason: “every way of a man is right in his own eyes, but Yahweh weighs the hearts” (Pro 21:2), and “there is a way that is right before a man, but its end is the ways of death” (Pro 14:12; 16:25). Each king is weighed by one measure, whether he did “the right in the eyes of Yahweh” as David, who “kept my commandments … to do only the right in my eyes” (1Ki 14:8; 15:11; 2Ki 22:2), or did not (2Ki 16:2). Jesus said, “I always do the things pleasing to him” (Joh 8:29), and John writes that “we keep his commandments and do the things pleasing before him” (1Jn 3:22), the Septuagint's words for doing what is right in Yahweh's eyes. From the verses: what is right is fixed by Yahweh's judgment and his commandments, not by a man's own sense of it, which can lead to death while it seems right.

Yahweh is upright: “a God of faithfulness and without injustice, righteous and upright is he” (Deu 32:4); “Yahweh is upright; my rock, and there is no unrighteousness in him” (Psa 92:16); his word, precepts and judgments are upright (Psa 33:4; 19:9; 119:137), and his ways are right, so that “the righteous walk in them, but transgressors stumble in them” (Hos 14:10). In the next verse of the song Israel is “a crooked and twisted generation” (Deu 32:5). “God made man upright, but they have sought out many schemes” (Ecc 7:29). Because Yahweh is good and upright, “therefore he instructs sinners in the way” (Psa 25:8). From the verses: man was made straight and turned himself crooked; the straightness is Yahweh's, and the way back to it is his instruction.

The psalms say that Yahweh “will judge the world in righteousness; he will judge the peoples with equity (בְּמֵישָׁרִים)” (Psa 9:9), and that this is when “he comes to judge the earth” (Psa 96:10, 13; 98:9). The shoot from the stump of Jesse “shall judge the poor with righteousness, and decide with equity (בְּמִישׁוֹר) for the meek of the earth” (Isa 11:1, 4), and the king of Psalm 45 holds “a sceptre of uprightness” (Psa 45:7). Hebrews quotes that psalm of the Son, and goes on, “therefore God, your God, has anointed you” (Heb 1:8–9; Psa 45:8): the king is anointed by his God. Paul told Athens that God “has appointed a day in which he will judge the world in righteousness by a man whom he has appointed, having given assurance to all by raising him from the dead” (Act 17:31), the psalms' own words. From the verses: the equity the psalms foretold is the judgment of the earth by Jesus, a man raised from the dead and anointed by his God, when he comes to reign.

“The upright will dwell in the land, and the blameless will remain in it; but the wicked will be cut off from the land” (Pro 2:21–22). Of those who trust in themselves the psalm says, “like sheep they are laid in the grave (שְׁאוֹל); death shall shepherd them, and the upright shall rule over them in the morning”, and then, “God will redeem my soul from the hand of the grave, for he will take me” (Psa 49:15–16). “The upright shall behold his face” (Psa 11:7); “the upright shall dwell before your face” (Psa 140:14); “mark the blameless and see the upright, for the end of that man is peace” (Psa 37:37). Balaam, looking at Israel, said, “let me die the death of the upright, and let my end be like his” (Num 23:10). From the verses: the upright die and go to the grave as other men, but their end is not there; in the morning they are redeemed from the grave to rule and to dwell in the land before Yahweh's face.

BDB keys assigned: j.dz.aa verb, j.dz.ab adjective, j.dz.ac יֹשֶׁר, j.dz.ae יְשָׁרָה, j.dz.ag מֵישָׁר, j.dz.ah מִישׁוֹר, j.dz.ai שָׁרוֹן, j.dz.aj שָׁרוֹנִי; the names in names/: j.dz.af jeshurun, j.dz.ad jesher. The zero-token cross-references l.cd.ae (לַשָּׁרוֹן), m.bw.ag and m.dy.aj (מֵישָׁרִים, מֵשָׁרִים) and v.gb.ae (שָׁרוֹנִי) are left unassigned. Asarelah's variant יְשַׂרְאֵלָה (1Ch 25:14), listed among the brief's leads, is spelled with sin and not taken here. Job 37:3 יִשְׁרֵהוּ, counted as a qal of this verb, is שָׁרָה “let loose” (Aramaic שְׁרָא) and is not cited. Psa 5:9 הַיְשַׁר (Qere; Ketiv הוֹשַׁר) is cited under the hiphil though the brief does not count it; Isa 45:2 אֲיַשֵּׁר is the Qere (Ketiv אוֹשִׁר, hiphil). Dan 11:17 וִישָׁרִים עִמּוֹ (“upright terms”? “upright ones”?) is left uncited pending a decision. The Septuagint renders Jeshurun ἠγαπημένος “beloved” (Deu 32:15; 33:5, 26; Isa 44:2), no evidence of the Hebrew; noted in names/jeshurun. No Biblical Aramaic or Peshitta word: SEDRA has no ܝܫܪ root, and Syriac and the Targums say “straight, upright” with ܬܪܝܨ / תְּרִיץ. Leads not followed: Ugaritic yšr “uprightness” (DULAT, not vendored; Ugaritic keeps ṯ apart, so it would confirm š); Phoenician ישר “just, legitimate” in royal inscriptions (Krahmalkov); CAD for ešēru and mīšaru beyond Oracc's glosses. Arabic وثر (waṯara “be smooth, plain”) was tried by sound correspondence: its ṯ is the wrong sound for the Aramaic š, so it is not recorded. Open questions: (1) whether Arabic yasara “be easy, gentle” belongs (recorded as possible); (2) whether Sharon is from this root at all: the text shows only pasture, never level ground; (3) the doctrine statements are reasoned conclusions to review.
